prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 5 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One painted storyboard image with five portrait 9:16 panels arranged three across and two down, read left to right; the bottom-right cell remains blank. No lettering, numbers, captions, arrows or logos appear anywhere. Kasun is a smooth, featureless red artist's mannequin of medium height and lean, wiry build; Anudi is a smooth, featureless blue mannequin of average height and slender build. The surroundings and props are realistic: rain-wet patched asphalt, narrow concrete pavement, open kerb drainage, weathered concrete commercial buildings, a dark-green three-wheeler with a black canopy, and subdued amber shop lamps beneath a blue awning. Soft overcast early-morning daylight comes from upper camera-left, with low contrast, muted grey and beige surfaces, restrained greens and gentle warm reflections. Anudi carries an open navy folding umbrella in her left hand and a structured tan handbag on her right shoulder, with brass-coloured fittings and an open exterior side pocket. The phone has an orange back, a transparent case and the camera arrangement shown in its reference.

Geography: The road and walking edge run horizontally from screen left to screen right, with every camera remaining on the road side of the action axis. The three-wheeler occupies the left-hand vending bay beside the modest concrete building; its rear wheel stands near the open drain and the phone's landing patch. Anudi's route continues right from this bay along the narrow pavement, past a long stain-streaked beige boundary wall with a dark concrete cap, toward adjoining shuttered shopfronts. Kasun follows the same route into the approach zone and then the meeting zone farther right. The continuous open drain stays on the lower-left side of the compositions, while the capped boundary wall links the bay, approach and meeting backgrounds; the vehicle and blue-awning shop recede toward frame left as the camera positions advance.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing eye height at the road-side pavement edge, looking across the route with a slight diagonal toward the shops; wide, 28mm feel, deep focus, full figures. Background: The parked three-wheeler and blue-awning shop occupy frame left. The stained, dark-capped boundary wall extends behind Anudi toward frame right; the open drain lies along the lower-left foreground. The red Kasun mannequin stands beside the three-wheeler on the left third, chest and head facing screen right in profile, with both hands resting beside his body. The blue Anudi mannequin is mid-step just to his right, travelling across the frame toward screen right, her chest and head aligned with her route. Her left hand holds the open umbrella above her, while her right hand holds the orange phone immediately outside the handbag's side pocket; the wet landing patch beside the rear wheel is empty.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — At kerb height on the same road side, looking slightly upward across Anudi's rightward path; low wide shot, 35mm feel, with her hand and the landing patch sharp. Background: The three-wheeler's rear wheel and open drain anchor frame left. The capped beige wall sits behind the walking edge, with shuttered frontages extending toward frame right; Kasun is outside the crop. The blue Anudi mannequin occupies the right third in a rightward stride, chest and head facing screen right rather than into the depth of the street. Her left hand holds the umbrella shaft with the canopy low above her, and her right hand still holds the orange phone at the open side pocket of the bag on her right shoulder. The rear wheel fills the left edge, with an unobstructed patch of wet asphalt between it and her feet; the phone is not yet on the ground.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — At standing height on the road side, angled down toward Kasun's lower torso, hands and feet; 50mm medium-detail framing, with his head outside the upper crop. Background: Three-wheeler bodywork borders frame left, with a narrow piece of the capped wall behind it at upper left. Wet pavement fills the remaining background, and the open drain remains at lower left. The red Kasun mannequin stands with his chest oriented screen right, his lower torso and legs filling the panel above the orange phone lying beside his right foot. His right hand hangs empty beside his thigh, and his left hand rests beside his opposite hip; both knees remain straight at this opening instant. The phone's orange back and clear case are plainly visible on the wet surface, just inside the kerb beside the vehicle.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height, positioned ahead and on the road side of Kasun, looking diagonally back toward the bay; medium chest-up framing, 35mm feel, three-quarter front view with rightward screen travel. Background: The blue awning and a small portion of the three-wheeler recede at far frame left. The same dark-capped beige wall runs behind Kasun on the left, newer shuttered frontage occupies frame right, and the drain remains visible at the lower-left edge. The red Kasun mannequin is caught in a forward-leaning running pose across the frame toward screen right, his chest presented in three-quarter view and his head aligned with his route. His right elbow is bent, holding the orange phone securely at the lower-right edge of the panel, while his empty left hand is raised beside his lower torso. Clear space remains ahead of him on frame right, with Anudi outside the frame.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Standing eye height on the road side, squared across the walking route; medium two-shot, 50mm feel, keeping both figures and the phone sharp. Background: The last section of the same capped beige wall remains behind Kasun at frame left, with adjoining shop shutters behind Anudi at frame right. The continuous open drain occupies the lower-left edge; the three-wheeler is now outside the frame to the left. The blue Anudi mannequin stands at frame right with chest and head still facing screen right in profile, her left hand holding the umbrella above her and her empty right hand beside the handbag on her right shoulder. The red Kasun mannequin enters from frame left in a shortened rightward step, chest and head directed toward her. His right forearm reaches forward with the orange phone, elbow still partly bent, while his empty left hand stays beside his body; a clear gap separates the phone from Anudi.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
